PG.rationale: PG is a fundamentally sound, wide-moat consumer staples franchise with excellent brand portfolio, strong cash generation, and a 70-year dividend increase streak. However, the near-term trajectory is mixed: Q3 FY2026 showed a welcome return to volume growth (+2% YoY) and beat estimates, but QoQ trends are negative (revenue -4.4%, EPS -8.4%), operating margins are compressing (21.5% vs 23.3% YoY), and management guided toward the lower end of its full-year range due to tariff and commodity headwinds. The $1B after-tax oil headwind estimate for FY2027 is a material concern. Valuation at ~23x P/E is near the lower end of its 1-year range (21.7-26.7), suggesting some compression has occurred, but it is not dramatically cheap versus its own history. The stock is down ~8% from its 52-week high and ~7.9% over the last quarter, reflecting some of these headwinds. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists beyond the July FY2027 guidance update, which carries significant uncertainty given the Middle East situation. The score reflects a quality franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation with modest headwinds, but no compelling re-rating catalyst.
